heading: Falcon Way Improvements
body: Mobile-friendly project updates for people checking Falcon Way Improvements from a phone. Find current notices, typical working hours, access-impact guidance, and who to contact.

label: Typical hours
heading: 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday to Friday
Traffic impacts section added
body: A new Traffic Impacts section now shows the current traffic implementation, the next planned implementation, and the timeline for each when approved.

heading: Communication guidance added
body: This bulletin now includes working hours, advance notice expectations, access-impact guidance, and public contact paths from the project communication process.

heading: How residents will be notified
body: Planned access, parking, traffic, waste collection, water, sewer, or utility impacts will be shared through direct notices such as door hangers, mail drops, or TFN-approved channels when required.

heading: Project QR code and website
body: The same QR code can stay active for the project and direct mobile users to current approved notices, updates, and contacts.

heading: Public project page published
body: The Falcon Way Improvements bulletin was published as a simple public website for mobile access.

label: Current
heading: Current traffic implementation
body: No active lane closure, detour, or traffic-control implementation has been posted to this bulletin yet. Follow site signage and traffic-control personnel when work is active.

label: Next
heading: Next traffic implementation
body: The next planned traffic setup and dates will be posted once approved, including expected duration and affected access or travel routes.

heading: Project purpose
body: Falcon Way Improvements will be delivered with focus on safety, respectful communication, resident access, traffic management, and coordination on Tsawwassen First Nation lands.

heading: What this bulletin covers
body: Use this page for approved public updates, current notices, upcoming work activities, traffic and access impacts, working hours, contact information, and safety or traffic reminders.

heading: How updates are shared
body: Updates may be posted here as project conditions change. Required direct notices will still be delivered by door hanger, mail drop, direct notice, or another TFN-approved channel.

heading: Review before posting
body: Information involving major traffic impacts, utility disruptions, private resident matters, or TFN coordination will be reviewed with the appropriate representatives before publication.

heading: Working hours
body: Standard working hours are 7:30 AM to 5:30 PM, Monday to Friday, unless otherwise approved by TFN or required for emergency work.

heading: Access and traffic impacts
body: For driveway, parking, access, traffic, waste collection, or similar impacts, the target is at least 48 hours' notice, with 72 hours where practical.

heading: Major or utility impacts
body: Major utility disruptions or total road closures target 5 business days' notice where practical. Water or sewer disruptions require separate notice at least 72 hours in advance.

heading: During active work
body: Follow posted traffic control, site signage, and resident access instructions. Contact the project team if a planned access need is affected.

heading: General project questions
body: For schedule questions, project limits, public notices, or general information, contact Kyle Palmer, Lead Project Coordinator.

label: urgent
heading: Urgent access or field concern
body: For driveway access, deliveries, parking, waste collection, noise, or other time-sensitive field concerns, contact the on-site escalation lead or project superintendent.

heading: Site coordination
body: For construction sequencing or site coordination, contact the Amrize site superintendent.

label: urgent
heading: Emergency or immediate safety risk
body: For police, fire, ambulance, injury, fire, or immediate public safety concerns, call emergency services first.

heading: Public notice reminder
body: This website supports the project QR code and central updates. It does not replace required direct resident notices or formal TFN/project communication channels.
